title: Linux Kernel Tracing & eBPF with BCC / Python (PYTH_187_S1 to PYTH_187_S8)

slides.title: eBPF Observability with BCC
slides.prompt: eBPF allows developers to run sandboxed C programs directly inside the Linux kernel, using Python for user-space control and metrics extraction.

slides.title: Initializing BCC BPF Object
slides.prompt: Fill in the BCC class used to compile and load inline eBPF C code into the kernel.

slides.title: Kprobes vs Uprobes
slides.prompt: What is the difference between a `kprobe` and a `uprobe` in Linux system instrumentation?
options: Kprobes instrument kernel-level function entries, while uprobes instrument user-space executable binaries
Kprobes inspect network sockets, while uprobes inspect disk files
Kprobes require Python 2, while uprobes require Python 3
Kprobes run on ARM CPUs, while uprobes run on x86 CPUs
slides.correctAnswer: Kprobes instrument kernel-level function entries, while uprobes instrument user-space executable binaries

slides.title: eBPF Map Data Structures
slides.prompt: Fill in the BCC macro term used inside kernel C code to share hash map data with Python user-space.

slides.title: eBPF In-Kernel Verification
slides.prompt: Why does the Linux kernel run an internal eBPF Verifier before executing loaded bytecode programs?
options: To guarantee memory safety, prevent infinite loops, and ensure the kernel cannot crash
To compile Python code into standard x86 assembly
To check if the user has an active cloud subscription
To format output logs as standard JSON
slides.correctAnswer: To guarantee memory safety, prevent infinite loops, and ensure the kernel cannot crash

slides.title: Attaching Uprobes to Python
slides.prompt: Fill in the BCC method used to attach user-level dynamic probes to standard shared C libraries or binaries.

slides.title: eBPF Perf Ring Buffers
slides.prompt: What is the primary benefit of using `BPF_PERF_OUTPUT` ring buffers over `bpf_trace_printk` for data submission?
options: High-throughput, low-overhead binary event streaming directly to user-space Python consumers
Storing events permanently in PostgreSQL database tables
Eliminating the need for root user privileges
slides.correctAnswer: High-throughput, low-overhead binary event streaming directly to user-space Python consumers

slides.title: Reading Kernel Trace Pipe
slides.prompt: Fill in the BCC method used in Python to continuously print standard debug trace logs from kernel space.
